Subject: Order Form: tiered rebate schedule + stability clause — redline review

Jake — thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Attached is our baseline order form with the pricing exhibit updated to reflect the tiered rebate language we discussed (see Valence_Exhibit_Pricing_v3.docx). Key items we flagged for legal review: 

- Tier breakpoints and lookback period for true-ups (Q over Q vs trailing 12).
- A 90‑day stabilization clause that limits mid‑term upward adjustments to unit price if Valence usage dips by more than 30% (you proposed 45%).
- A capped rebate pool for overage credits so that per-quarter rebates cannot exceed 20% of committed spend.

Can you confirm whether the stabilization clause as written (section 3.2) is acceptable, or provide specific counter-language from your side? If you prefer, we can island out the clause into an addendum to speed signature.

I’ve looped in Aditya (pricing) and Laura (legal approvals) to weigh in on concessions and the minimal guardrails we need for committed revenue recognition.

Thanks,
Monica

Subject: Re: Order Form: tiered rebate schedule + stability clause — redline review

Monica — appreciate the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet; attached is our annotated redline (Valence_OrderForm_Redline_annotated.pdf). High-level summary: 

- Stabilization clause: Valence requests the stabilization threshold be 50% (we need more runway on seasonal rolloffs) and that any upward adjustment be limited to 10% of unit price per quarter, not instant re‑pricing.
- Rebate pool cap: we asked for a 30% cap tied to the prior 4Q average rather than fixed committed spend to avoid penalizing growth helpers.
- Lookback window: proposed 180-day trailing window for true-ups to smooth short spikes.

We can accept a single addendum for the stabilization language if Redwood includes an explicit exception for scheduled product decommissioning and for extraordinary pandemic-like events.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call Monday to walk through line-by-line.

Best,

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form: tiered rebate schedule + stability clause — redline review

Monica/Laura — reviewed Jake’s annotated redline and ran the scenarios in the attached pricing-model worksheet. Short summary and recommended tradeoffs: 

- Stabilization threshold: moving from 30% -> 50% materially increases revenue volatility risk; with a 50% threshold, our downside exposure in low-util quarters rises ~18% in the model. Recommendation: agree to 45% threshold (split the diff) with the conditional quarterly cap of 10% upward reprice (Valence asked; we can accept 10% if we get guardrails below).
- Rebate cap: switching to a 4Q average basis instead of committed spend reduces predictability for forecasting. Recommendation: keep a cap tied to committed spend but allow a ‘growth buffer’ exception — i.e., the first 20% overcommit in a rolling year is excluded from the rebate calculation.
- Lookback window: 180-day trailing is reasonable operationally. Acceptable if true-up invoices are netted and applied only in next billing cycle.

If we accept Aditya’s recommended compromise (45% stabilization, 10% quarterly cap, committed-spend cap with 20% growth buffer, 180d lookback), legal should incorporate a two-paragraph addendum and a one‑page exhibit table showing calculation examples. Laura — can you draft minimal addendum language that is signature‑ready?

If Valence insists on 50% or the 30% -> 50% jump, we’d need a concession on minimum annual committed spend or a shorter rebate payout window.

Thanks — I’ll prep the demo schedule for Monday if Jake wants a walkthrough.

Cheers,
Aditya
Director, Pricing & Packaging | Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, contracts@valencehealth.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: tiered rebate schedule + stability clause — redline review

Jake — thanks for the redline and for surfacing the sensitivity on lookbacks. We’ve reviewed internally and can accept a compromise to advance to signature: 

- Stabilization threshold: 45% (middle ground).
- Upward adjustment cap: 10% per quarter with a 90-day notice window before implementation; any uplift applied to new invoices only.
- Rebate pool cap: tied to committed spend but with a 20% growth buffer exemption for the first rolling year.
- Lookback/true-ups: 180-day trailing window; true-ups netted on next invoice.

Laura will circulate a short addendum + a one‑page illustrative exhibit for countersignature by Monday EOD. Once Valence signs the addendum we’ll prepare the order form for DocuSign. If you need the addendum to be incorporated into the master order form instead, please flag ASAP.

Otherwise, we appreciate the flexibility — happy to take the 30-min call if you want to go line-by-line.

Best regards,
Monica
